meta.title: The High Routes
meta.description: High Route 1 of the Giants and High Route 2 of the Shepherds: the official multi-day routes of Aosta Valley with stage data and maps.

AlteVie.heroEyebrow: Official routes — Aosta Valley Autonomous Region
AlteVie.heroSubtitle: The High Routes are the official multi-day itineraries of Aosta Valley: waymarked regional routes crossing the region from east to west, linking Walser villages, historic refuges and cols above 2,700 m. Unlike Tours — loops around a single massif — the High Routes tell the full story of the Aosta Valley in one traverse. Born in the 1970s as a hiking alternative to mass tourism, they remain among the most complete alpine treks in Europe, with a refuge network, CAI waymarking and official data from the regional trail registry.
AlteVie.mapHint: Official VdA Region GPX tracks · use zoom and compass to explore
AlteVie.compareSubtitle: AV1 crosses the three great massifs on the northern flank; AV2 follows the southern side with a naturalist focus and Gran Paradiso wildlife.

av1.name: High Route 1 — of the Giants
av1.description: High Route 1 crosses the entire Aosta Valley, touching all three great massifs — Monte Rosa, Matterhorn and Mont Blanc — in seventeen stages from the vineyards of Donnas (322 m) to the ridges above Courmayeur. It is the most complete alpine traverse in the region: Walser pastures, glacial lakes, historic refuges and panoramas from Gran Paradiso to Mont Blanc. Created in the 1970s as a hiking alternative to mountaineering routes, it is now the most popular multi-day route in the valley, with impeccable waymarking and a well-distributed refuge network. This site covers all 17 stages with GPX, elevation profiles, geology and verified practical data.

av2.name: High Route 2 — Naturalistica
av2.route: Courmayeur → Donnas (southern flank, right orographic bank)
av2.description: The Naturalistica High Route crosses the southern flank of Aosta Valley — Val Veny, La Thuile, Valgrisenche, Rhêmes, Valsavarenche, Cogne and Champorcher — with outstanding wildlife in Gran Paradiso and Mont Avic parks. First section of the Tor des Géants route. This site covers all 14 stages with data verified from lovevda.it and the official trail registry.
av2.sources: Sources: lovevda.it, VdA Trail Registry, Wikipedia

AlteVie.legalNote: High Routes 1 and 2 are official waymarked routes of the Aosta Valley Autonomous Region. The numbering (AV1, AV2) is official. Massif Tours (TMB, Tour Monte Rosa, etc.) are distinct routes listed in the <tourLink>Tours section</tourLink>.

meta.title: The Tours
meta.description: Tour of Mont Blanc, Monte Rosa, Matterhorn, Gran Paradiso, Rutor and Grand Combin: hiking loops around the great Aosta Valley massifs.

Tour.heroSubtitle: Tours are hiking loops circling a massif, often crossing borders and multiple valleys. Unlike High Routes — which traverse Aosta Valley from east to west — Tours follow the rim of a single mountain group. The Tour du Mont Blanc (TMB) is the world's most famous; other Valdostan routes offer wilder, quieter alternatives around Rosa, Matterhorn, Gran Paradiso, Rutor and Grand Combin.
Tour.mapHint: Official GPX tracks · use zoom and compass to explore

tmb.name: Tour du Mont Blanc (TMB)
tmb.places: Courmayeur, Rif. Bertone (2,011 m), Rif. Bonatti (2,025 m), Rif. Elena (2,062 m), La Fouly (CH)
tmb.description: The most famous route in the Alps: ten full days, three countries, constant views of the south face of Mont Blanc. The Italian section in Val Ferret — from Courmayeur to Rifugio Bonatti — is considered the most spectacular on the entire loop, with Grandes Jorasses and the Miage glacier.

monteRosa.name: Tour of Monte Rosa
monteRosa.description: A loop around the second highest massif in the Alps, crossing Walser valleys, Lys glaciers and passes above 2,700 m. The Valdostan section links Gressoney, Ayas and Valsesia in a route less crowded than the TMB but equally grand.

cervino.name: Tour of the Matterhorn
cervino.description: Circles the most iconic pyramid in the Alps, alternating Italian and Swiss valleys. The Valdostan side offers Plateau Rosa, huts above Valtournenche and head-on Matterhorn views matched by few other trails.

granParadiso.name: Tour of Gran Paradiso
granParadiso.description: A loop entirely within Gran Paradiso National Park: Cogne, Valsavarenche and Valle dell'Orco (Piedmont). Outstanding wildlife — ibex almost guaranteed — and a landscape studied by glaciologists as a laboratory of alpine climate change.

rutor.name: Tour of Rutor
rutor.description: One of the lesser-known tours but among the most accessible for observing an active glacier. The loop around Rutor, above La Thuile, combines quiet summer farms, glacial lakes and views of the western Mont Blanc massif.

granCombin.name: Tour of Grand Combin
granCombin.description: A massif less known to the general public but glaciologically spectacular: the cross-border loop crosses Valpelline and the Swiss side with passes above 2,700 m and views of Combin de Grafeneire.
